correctness.rationale: The exact cardinal replacement and nodal-product identities yield a uniform two-sided 1/|m| tail near the shifted node with coefficient |sin(pi*u)|*|1-tau/u|/pi. The intermediate-index errors sum to O(1), and distant terms are O(1); the intact-grid bound and rank-one correction localize every maximum. Strict concavity and endpoint derivative signs produce the unique optimizer. The standalone checker passed 195 supplementary finite assertions. Limits and uniqueness follow from proof, not tests.

originality.rationale: The verified 2026 motivating paper proves a smaller worst-case sufficient shift scale and a distinct two-node near-collision obstruction; it does not give this one-node fixed-fraction logarithmic coefficient. The two most relevant indexed published complete results were inspected: one deletes a node and drops degree, while the other optimizes periodic robust certificates. Search queries for equivalents, stronger coverage, parameter aliases and finite tables revealed no implication covering the exact one-defect asymptotic, subject to the recorded older full-text priority risks.
residual_risks: A classical single-defect interpolation theorem may express an equivalent result via barycentric weights or rank-one sampling updates.
Austin–Trefethen 2017 and Piazzon–Vianello 2018 publisher full texts were not obtained; their subject matter is distinct as discussed, but direct section-by-section exclusion is unavailable.
Negative search results cannot certify exhaustive publication priority.

value.rationale: Accurate error amplification for a single displaced sample is a natural calibration/stability problem at a scale where the existing worst-case theorem is silent. The new exact log coefficient is nontrivial (strictly larger than 2/pi for every positive fraction), independent of the defect bulk location, and accompanied by a uniquely determined limiting worst evaluation point. This sharp classification is of use even without a general multiple-node theorem.
